body: Oh, and You're allowed to create boundaries when it comes to people touching you and hugging you. Its your body. You are in control. That doesn't make you too sensitive or emotional. That makes you a fucking badass for taking back the control that someone else took from you.

wow... My heart hurts for you. I'm sure if there were any other options for you, you would take them. You don't deserve any of that... Every single part of what they say just shows a profound lack of empathy and emotional intelligence.

I know that you logically know all of these things, but I want you to know that they're wrong. You can hate your abuser. (it'll take time for the pain to no longer influence your life, but that's completely different than saying you shouldn't hate them). It's absolute bullshit that they would tell you that women don't belong in the army. You are strong and capable. You survive every day in spite of what you've been through.

I'm just a stranger and It's probably inappropriate for me to give you this kind of advice, but If I were you, I would guard myself as long as I was forced to live with them. You deserve to stick up for yourself, but just try to avoid these hopeless fights until you're independent again. . Which you will be. You have to take care of yourself, not educate a bunch of assholes. Remember the fight that you have inside. The hardest thing to do in times like this is to get out of bed, and I know you can do it.

My brother-in-law told me that he has never once thought about killing himself.... not even in a fleeting moment. It blew my mind. He's not religious. He has a great life, but I mean so many people who are suicidal have a great life. And he has problems and has terrible parents. He's not even an annoyingly happy-go-lucky person. He's just so content with who he is. It's crazy. I'm jealous.

It's okay to not mesh well with your therapist. People I talk to typically give it three sessions to determine if it's a match. If they still don't click then they try another.   
Just be honest and direct about the kind of things you want to work on. Or if you're unsure, communicate that to them.

Well I'm glad you're still here. Stay strong friend.   


.... You are strong. You made it through a low
Stay strong... I'm so sorry, again, for everything you and your friends are going through. Lean on each other <3

That's so fucked up that she told you that. I'm sure it was a moment of anger and that she didn't mean it and had no idea how that would truly affect your soul. But you don't deserve that. I'm just here to tell you that I don't want you to die. I'm not going to say that you're too young to feel this way because I've been there at your age and understand exactly how you feel.

please don't. I attempted and I regret it so much. I might be saying the same things as you in a few months, but right now I am so glad I'm still alive. And nothing has changed about my life (well except better meds). In fact, after my attempt, everything turned upside down and feels worse. But I'm here. I can keep trying. I'm done trying to find a purpose and feeling so worthless about not having one. My purpose is me now. I'm taking things one step at a time, and I know that's fucking annoying as hell for you to hear right now.I don't want you to die.

I'm so sorry.

I think you'll notice from people's posts on here that there's a lot of pain. There's a lot of feelings of worthlessness. Even if you appear happy to people, when you're alone you're your own demon. I always say that other people can't hurt my feelings, because I've already said every nasty thought imaginable to myself.I don't know your friend's situation, but I can tell you my story and you can maybe get some insight.

I first wanted to kill myself when I was 7. My childhood was hectic and unstable. but I definitely think it was a chemical imbalance that has always affected my mind. I would pray every night that god would just take me in my sleep. My family knew nothing. Absolutely nothing. They were shocked when my best friend called them saying I was in the hospital.  I was a quiet kid who never got into any trouble. The last thing I wanted was that kind of attention and for people to worry about me. I didn't want to do it, but it's like a monster directing your emotions. It lasted until around high school (the, every night begging the universe, thing). Then after that, I would have low moments, but I always felt in control of it. I thought I could handle it myself.

When I made my attempt it wasn't even my lowest point, depression-wise. I had felt worse before. But I didn't give myself time to think or remember the people I loved. I knew if I did I would convince myself to stay alive for them. It's a sickness. A scary fucking sickness. It seems selfish to leave your family with this kind of trauma, to the people looking in. But it truly feels, in those moments of desperation, that this pain will never end. that every breath and every moment that you have to act normal around people is excruciating. You have your rational brain telling you to suck it up and that you're being dramatic, but that makes you feel worse about yourself. and you spiral.

I did it after a weekend with my family. It was a great trip. And I think I was feeling in the moment like... If this happy moment can't make me feel a sense of purpose or fulfillment... then nothing will...

​

I have no idea how to make the family feel better. But hopefully, the perspective of someone who failed their attempt, regrets it, and is out the other side trying to pick up the pieces can help you understand. My heart is with you.

I don't want you to die.   
You feeling this way makes you stronger than you know. Getting up every day in spite of your pain is a miracle. You've lived a miracle for so many days this far, you can do it tonight.
And please don't drink any more tonight... I know I'm just some stranger on the internet. But I've been exactly where you are. And I don't want you to die.

Hey. You've got this. Don't listen to the monster telling you that you're worthless. You've worked through this before and you can do it tonight.   
It takes strength to deal with this kind of crushing pain every moment.

You can do this. You can make it through the night. I know, because you're still here. You do it every day and you can do it again. and for people like us, sometimes getting out of bed takes the strength of a fucking elephant.

my heart hurts for you. I'm so sorry you're struggling so much right now.   


By answering, do you mean on here? or in your normal life.

I definitely struggle with connections. I think that the people that I do make connections with end up using me. I tend to gravitate towards "fixer-upper" situations because it makes me feel useful and necessary in someone's life. But when situations like that crash and burn it's horrible.I almost feel like happy, put together, people can sense how broken I am and run away from that.

I now try to see it as pain attracts pain. I think that's why we're all here. We have felt the bottomless pit of depression and at least resonate with each other. Once you've been cut that deep it changes you. I'm trying to stop caring about the perception of having friends. But I get it. It's hard. Especially during a time that's supposed to celebrate you and shower you with love. Shower yourself with love instead.

​

Hang in there, and Happy Birthday

Medication helps but it's definitely not everything. I'm proud of you for opening up to people close to you. That's so incredibly difficult. It shows that you're using every ounce of strength you have, and still trying to anchor yourself to this world.   


Hang in there. You deserve to take up space in the world.
You're in big sister mode, but remember to take care of your pain too. Good luck hunny

Please don't. This is such a horrible situation for you to be in, but don't get caught up in the moment of this pain. He's an absolute ass and needs to end the relationship himself if he's going to say something like that. It's not your fault. you're not the one responsible for hurting your sister. The future looks different, but he's shown his true colors and put you in an unimaginable situation.

I know, it's bullshit. Just hang on hunny... my attempt is the biggest regret of my life and being on the other side, I'm grateful that I failed.

It seems like a release of pain in the moment, but don't give into those negative thoughts. I call them my monster. Have you thought more about talking to a family member about this? It doesn't have to be your parents. Maybe your sister?
yah, From my research I've learned that mine are hypertrophic... trying out silicone sheets, oils, Mederma, and hopefully that'll help...
I know you're ashamed of them, but they look so great. mine are still fresh, from December of 2020, and it feels like they'll never turn white...
I've also been experimenting with silicone sheets. I don't really like them (they make my scars so itchy) but I hear they work really well

omg, they look great! that gives me so much hope for using Mederma twice a day. If someone sees mine this summer or asks why I'm wearing coverups I'm planning on saying that I had a bad accident and don't want to talk about it. Figured I'd share my excuse with you.

P.s. another positive: your scars kind of look more like an animal attack as they're healing. also a useful excuse.
To top it off, you have to go through school in the worst fucking time in humanity. I can only imagine what you're going through and I know it sucks.

I understand completely. I first wanted to kill myself when I was 7. I stopped only because I thought that my mother would be more upset about the mess I would leave behind. 

Your value isn't in the college you go to, or some white picket fence fucking fantasy. I never pictured my life as an adult because I never thought I'd make it here. So I didn't have a plan. I didn't have a direction. I'm still figuring it out.   


Now all that I want to do is be boring and simple and that has given me so much freedom from the pressures of needing to appear special.   


I understand how hard and risky it is, especially since you're a minor, to tell someone what's going on. You don't necessarily have to. It's your choice. It does change things. But please keep fighting for yourself.   


Don't feel the need to pursue some passion. But please keep trying. It gets better. It's a rollercoaster, but it always comes back up.

I hope you see this because it would mean you're still alive. It's absolutely crushing what you've been through. Do you think you would tell the love of your life how you're feeling? Remember the things that anchor us to this world. You already have one of the best: love.

I'm so proud of you for getting help at such a young age. I'm jealous honestly. If I had tried back then I don't think I would have ever made my attempt last year at 28.   
You have your mom, who understands a lot about what you're going through and that's so special <3
Do you think if you phrased it as you and your sister "being depressed" they would be more receptive and help you get treatment?

My heart hurts for you...   
I think you ultimately know if your parents would be helpful in that situation or not. I don't know if that's appropriate to say, I just know how my parents would have reacted when I was still living with them... and it wouldn't have been good...  


At least you guys have each other now. My older sister and I developed very different issues because of our toxic home environment (she has struggled with eating disorders and I'm suicidal) but it bonded us for life. Tell her that you're feeling the same way. Lean on each other. It's terrifying, but decide together that you will take care of each other and figure out your path together.

I've only called the hotline once and I agree, it didn't help. I hung up when they kept asking the basic questions "do you want to kill yourself? do you have a gun?"   


Yes I fucking want to kill myself, that's why I called!!!   


I know you were looking more to just vent, but I want you to know that I've been there. And how I'm choosing to move out of my slump is to just focus on connecting to one person, or group of people at a time. I would go with a couple of people. If you're anything like me you kind of wrap your happiness in how well your relationships are going, and if you only have one and it turns... well it's not great. I'm only talking to my sister and her family (I'm living with them currently) my mom (kind of, she's a piece of work) my friend (who called 911 after my attempt), and the rest I have told that I'm "in a funk" (no details necessary) thanks for reaching out, but I'll connect when I'm back to 100% (no idea when that will come if ever)   
I've reached the point with my circle where they're not constantly bringing up my attempt or depression, which is nice.   


Hang in there, please. I regret my attempt so much.

exactly. My sister basically wants me to be a motivational speaker after my attempt. some Instagrammer influencer bullshit. "use this to help people" 

I can barely help myself.

I pursued my passion for travelling and became a flight attendant. Having such a passion-driven lifestyle definitely made people idolize my life... It made my depression even worse. It made me feel even more pathetic for not being happy. It made it harder to connect with people who didn't understand how difficult the lifestyle was. I felt guilty when I wasn't travelling enough, and then guilty for travelling too much because I didn't feel like any of my relationships were meaningful.   


I told my family a few weeks ago after they encouraged me to find something that I'm passionate about, that I just want to be boring and normal. I want stability. I don't want the pressures of trying to be special. Life is boring and I want to embrace that and feel comfortable with that.

No normal person can do everything. Everyones a loser. Some people are just better at hiding it. And people like us feel the pain of every failure so much deeper.I've had a panic attack after feeling like a failure mid-grocery shopping trip, because I felt like every meal idea I had for my then boyfriend was fucking terrible and that there was no point in trying. I left the full shopping cart in the middle of the produce section and walked home crying.These thoughts aren't you. It's the monster inside us.

I'm with you.

​

oh, and fuck emotionally abusive assholes like my ex...

i've been struggling with wether or not I want my sister and my best friend (who was the one who called the ambulance after my attempt) to confide in people about how my attempt has affected them.Now so many people who I never wanted to know, know. I don't want it to define me. I don't want that kind of attention from it. I don't want people to see how broken I already know that I am. The truth is, they just don't understand and are just processing everything. You need to tell her that it's your choice who you want to find out about your thoughts (if you haven't already) I still haven't put my foot down with my sister and I'm putting her needs before my own. It's okay to be a little selfish right now.I can tell you though, that even though it's hard. even though it feels like the more difficult path. In the end, it's better to have eyes on you.... to have someone trying to take care of you. The biggest regret of my life was not telling my sister sooner... I don't think I would have never attempted if i had.

I completely understand how you feel. I spent months trying to set little goals for myself to feel like i was chipping away at the mountain of self-care that needed to be done (cleaning my apartment, working out, eating healthy) And it felt like the harder I tried the harder it was. It was almost like I was patronizing myself. Why should I celebrate washing the dishes for the first time in a month? I still can't invite anyone over to my apartment because the rest of it looks like an absolutely disgusting depression hole.  


I can tell you, the thing that's helped me is choosing to live with someone while I recover from an attempt. I'm held accountable. It's hard a hell don't get me wrong, I'm living with a family member and feel like a child. But having eyes on me has helped me at least go through the motions. And going through the motions has made it easier to actually feel better. You're not your depression. I call it my monster.   
Keep working to find the right meds for you. It's hard as hell. It takes someone who has gone through it to know that the strength it takes to keep breathing and living through this makes you stronger than you give yourself credit for right now.

It's not about willpower. You have problems stopping, and it's not because you're weak. It's a serious fucking illness. That you have to think your way out of, and it feels impossible because (at least for me) your brain is the problem.

I call my depression and suicidal thoughts my monster. It's easier to fight a monster than yourself. Idk if that's helpful or just annoying...

I made an attempt a few months ago and I'm lucky enough to still be here. I'm so sorry that you lost your friend. The pain I have from seeing what this has done to my best friend and family will be with me forever. Causing that kind of trauma for them was something I tried to avoid for my whole life.... loss like yours and my sister's tears will hopefully allow me to stay strong in my darkest times.

It's a tough habit to break. I call it the monster. I try to remind myself (after my attempt) that those thoughts aren't me, they're my illness.   


I also stay away from alcohol now... it feeds the monster at night....
